extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners filing PCT (international) applications with the United States Receiving Office (USPTO); patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural quality requirements for preparing and filing an international (PCT) application at the USPTO (Receiving Office), including required elements, signatures, language, fees, document order/formatting, and handling of earlier searches and corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required elements of an international application
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application shall contain, as specified in the Treaty and the Regulations, a Request, a description, one or more claims, an abstract, and one or more drawings (where required). (PCT Art. 3(2) and Administrative Instructions Section 207.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements must be arranged in order: the request, the description (other than any sequence listing part), the claims, the abstract, the drawings, and the sequence listing part of the description (where applicable). Only one copy need be filed in the United States Receiving Office. (See PCT Article 3(2), Administrative Instructions Section 207, 37 CFR 1.433(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: International filing date: conditions for accord
rubrics_metrics.description: The receiving Office shall accord as the international filing date the date of receipt of the international application, provided that at the time of receipt certain requirements under PCT Article 11(1) were satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements include at least one applicant being a resident or national of the receiving Office's State, prescribed language, indication that it is intended as an international application, designation of at least one Contracting State, applicant name, a part appearing to be a description, and a part appearing to be a claim. If requirements are not satisfied on initial receipt, applicant is invited to correct within a set time; the filing date becomes the date of the timely correction. If correction not timely made, the RO will notify the applicant that the application is not an international application. If corrections are completely contained in an earlier application (with priority claim and proper incorporation), the initial receipt date may be retained. (See PCT Art. 11, PCT Rules 4.18, 20.3–20.6, 20.4.)

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO competence to act as Receiving Office
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will accord an international filing date only if at least one applicant is a United States resident or national and the papers so indicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no applicant is a U.S. resident or national, USPTO is generally not a competent RO under PCT Rule 19.1(a). However, the USPTO may receive the application on behalf of the International Bureau under Rule 19.4(a) and transmit it upon payment of a fee equal to the transmittal fee, provided at least one applicant is a resident or national of any PCT Contracting State. If all applicants are residents/nationals of non-PCT states, Rule 19.4 does not apply and no international filing date is accorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirement for receiving Office
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application must be in a prescribed language (for USPTO, English).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO is not competent to receive international applications that are not in English; upon payment of a fee equal to the transmittal fee, USPTO may forward such applications to the International Bureau under Rule 19.4 provided they are in a language accepted by the International Bureau as receiving Office. (See PCT Art. 3(4)(i), 35 U.S.C. 361(c), PCT Rule 4.2.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of States by filing an international application
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of a request shall constitute the designation of all Contracting States that are bound by the Treaty on the international filing date and indicate the kinds of protection sought (national/regional).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notwithstanding the all-inclusive designation, PCT Rule 4.9(b) permits certain exceptions where claiming priority to an earlier national application would cause the earlier application to cease effect in that State; affected States must have notified the IB. Some States (e.g., Germany, Japan, Republic of Korea) may be excluded by request in limited circumstances. (See PCT Rule 4.9 and 37 CFR 1.432.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of international filing, transmittal and search fees: timing and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment of the international filing fee and the transmittal and search fees may be made in full at the time the international application papers are deposited or within one month thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The payable fee is the fee in effect on the receipt date. If fees are not paid within one month and prior to sending a notice of deficiency (which imposes a late payment fee), applicant will be notified and given a one-month non-extendable time limit to pay the deficient fees plus the late payment fee. Failure to timely pay required fees (including pursuant to PCT Rule 16bis.1(e)) can lead the Receiving Office to declare the international application withdrawn under PCT Article 14(3)(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of deficiencies and effect on filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: If requirements under PCT Article 11(1) are not satisfied at initial receipt, the receiving Office will invite the applicant to correct the deficiency within a set time limit; the international filing date will be the date on which a timely filed correction is received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a defect is not timely corrected, the RO will notify that the application is not and will not be treated as an international application. If the defect is lack of a part that appears to be a description or claims but the initial receipt contained a priority claim and proper incorporation by reference, the initial receipt date may be retained if the submitted correction was completely contained in the earlier application (see PCT Rules 4.18 and 20.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: All sheets and risk to priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Where all sheets pertaining to the same international application are not received on the same day by the Receiving Office, the date of receipt will in most instances be amended to reflect the date on which the last missing sheets were received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amended date of receipt may cause the priority claim to be forfeited; applicants should ensure all sheets are deposited with the Receiving Office on the same day. If corrections are fully contained in an earlier application and a priority claim was present, the initial receipt date may nevertheless be retained (see PCT Rules 4.18, 20.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Order and numbering of parts and sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: The elements of the international application are to be arranged in the order: request, description (other than any sequence listing part), claims, abstract, drawings, and sequence listing part (if applicable). All sheets must be numbered in consecutive Arabic numerals using separate series: first series for the request; second for description, claims and abstract; third for drawings; further series for sequence listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use separate numbering series for different parts (PCT Rule 11.7 and Administrative Instructions Section 207(b)). Only one copy need be filed in the U.S. Receiving Office. Improper order or numbering may be corrected but following the prescribed order aids processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request form PCT/RO/101 and ePCT usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The Request shall be made on standardized form PCT/RO/101 or presented as a computer printout prepared using WIPO's ePCT system complying with the Administrative Instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Check List portion should indicate each accompanying document. The Request may not contain matter not specified in PCT Rules 4.1–4.17 or permitted under Rule 4.18(a); additional material will be deleted ex officio. ePCT validates entered data, creates a zip file, and electronic submission entitles applicant to a reduction of the international filing fee. Applicants using ePCT should be mindful of foreign filing license requirements for inventions made in the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: File reference format and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant or agent may indicate a file reference; it may be composed of letters of the Latin alphabet or Arabic numerals, or both, and may not exceed 25 characters including spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If file reference exceeds 25 characters, the Receiving Office may ex officio truncate it to 25 characters and notify the applicant. The Receiving Office, IB, ISA, and IPEA will use the file reference in correspondence with the applicant (Administrative Instructions Section 109, PCT Rule 11.6(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Date formatting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each date appearing in the international application or any correspondence must be indicated by the Arabic number of the day, the name of the month and the Arabic number of the year, in that order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the Request the date should be repeated in parentheses with a two-digit Arabic numeral each for day and month followed by the year in four digits, separated by periods, slashes or hyphens, e.g., '20 March 2020 (20.03.2020)'. (Administrative Instructions Section 110.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Title of invention requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Request must contain the title of the invention; the title must be short (preferably 2 to 7 words) and precise (PCT Rule 4.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The title in Box I is considered the title of the application and should be consistent with the title on the first page of the description and the abstract. The examiner should not change a title merely because it contains words not considered descriptive (e.g., 'improved'); if not descriptive, a change to a more descriptive title should be made and the applicant informed. Missing or inconsistent titles will prompt an invitation to correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Names formatting and content
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of a natural person must be indicated by the family name followed by the given name(s); academic degrees or titles must be omitted. The family name should preferably be written in capital letters. The name of a legal entity must be indicated by its full official designation (preferably in capital letters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow prescribed cultural/order conventions and avoid including non-name elements. See MPEP § 1806 regarding who can be an applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addresses content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses must be indicated so as to satisfy requirements for prompt postal delivery and must consist of all relevant administrative units up to and including house number (if any) and must include the country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete postal addresses to ensure communications are deliverable; incomplete addresses can impede correspondence and processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirements and who may sign
rubrics_metrics.description: The Request shall be signed by the applicant or, if there is more than one applicant, by all of them. For purposes of Article 14(1)(a)(i), if there is more than one applicant it is sufficient that the request be signed by one of them. The international application may also be signed by an agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handwritten signatures must meet 37 CFR 1.4(d)(1) requirements; S-signatures must comply with 37 CFR 1.4(d)(2) and patent practitioners using S-signatures must supply registration number either as part of the S-signature or immediately below/adjacent. If a person signs on behalf of a legal entity, their name and capacity should be indicated; proof of authority may be required if apparent authority is lacking (e.g., copy of board resolution, bylaws, delegation). A separate power of attorney may be waived by the RO in most cases. Lack of signature on Request is a correctable defect under PCT Article 14(1)(a)(i) and (b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority and acceptable titles for signers on behalf of legal entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons signing on behalf of a legal entity should indicate their name and capacity; officers such as President, Secretary, Treasurer, Chief Executive Officer, Chief Operating Officer or Chief Financial Officer are presumed to have authority. Titles that do not clearly indicate officer status generally are not presumed to confer authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof of authority is required if the signer does not possess apparent authority; acceptable proof includes board resolution, bylaws, or a separate delegation. For foreign juristic applicants, titles like 'Manager' or 'Director' may be acceptable as indicating authority due to differences in foreign practice; narrow titles such as 'Manager of Patents' may not be acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature by agent and practitioner registration numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application may be signed by an agent; a patent practitioner acting in a representative capacity must set forth his/her registration number on submitted papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: S-signature rules and the requirement to supply registration numbers help identify signatories; the RO will accept signatures meeting 37 CFR 1.4(d) handwritten or S-signature requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description sufficiency (enablement / disclosure)
rubrics_metrics.description: The description shall disclose the invention in a manner sufficiently clear and complete for the invention to be carried out by a person skilled in the art. (PCT Article 5.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The description should disclose the invention as claimed so that the technical problem and its solution can be understood and state advantageous effects relative to background art. It should set forth at least the best mode contemplated (where applicable) and indicate how the invention is capable of exploitation in industry and how it can be made and used (or only used if applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner and headings of the description
rubrics_metrics.description: The description shall first state the title and then: (i) specify the technical field; (ii) indicate the background art useful for understanding/searching/examination; (iii) disclose the invention as claimed such that problem and solution are understood; (iv) briefly describe figures; (v) set forth at least the best mode contemplated; (vi) indicate industrial applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specified manner and order should be followed except where a different order yields better understanding. Headings are suggested: 'Technical Field', 'Background Art', 'Disclosure of Invention' or 'Summary of Invention', 'Brief Description of Drawings', 'Best Mode for Carrying out the Invention' (or 'Description of Embodiments'), and 'Industrial Applicability' (PCT Rule 5.1, Administrative Instructions Section 204).

rubrics_metrics.name: Best mode disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The description shall set forth at least the best mode contemplated by the applicant for carrying out the invention claimed; this shall be done in terms of examples, where appropriate, and with reference to the drawings, if any. (PCT Rule 5.1(a)(v)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the national law of a designated State does not require best mode, failure to describe the best mode contemplated shall have no effect in that State. The MPEP notes that best mode should be presented in examples and with reference to drawings where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The description shall indicate explicitly, when it is not obvious from the description or nature of the invention, the way in which the invention is capable of exploitation in industry and the way in which it can be made and used, or, if it can only be used, the way in which it can be used. (PCT Rule 5.1(a)(vi)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'industry' is to be understood in its broadest sense as in the Paris Convention for the Protection of Industrial Property. Make explicit statements where exploitation is not obvious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taking into account results of an earlier search (request to ISA)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant wishes the International Searching Authority (ISA) to take into account the results of an earlier international, international-type or national search, the request shall indicate this and specify the Authority or Office concerned and the application in respect of which the earlier search was carried out. The request may also state that the international application is the same or substantially the same as that earlier application (PCT Rule 4.12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should identify earlier application(s) in Box No. VII of the Request by filing date, application number, and the country or regional Office. The USPTO performs an international-type search on all U.S. national applications filed on and after June 1, 1978; no specific applicant request is required for that.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of copies/translations of earlier search and earlier application
rubrics_metrics.description: Where Rule 4.12 is invoked, the applicant shall submit to the receiving Office, with the international application, a copy of the results of the earlier search in whatever form they are presented by the Authority or Office concerned (PCT Rule 12bis.1(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ISA may invite the applicant to furnish within a reasonable time: a copy of the earlier application, translations of the earlier application or search results where needed, and copies of any document cited in the earlier search results. Exceptions: if the earlier search was by the same Office/ISA or if a copy/translation is available to the ISA (e.g., digital library), submission may not be required. The applicant may request the Receiving Office prepare/transmit copies for a fee (Rule 12bis.1(c)–(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental box usage on Request form
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supplemental Box is used for any material which cannot be placed in one of the previous boxes because of space limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material in the supplemental box should be clearly entitled with the Box number being continued (e.g., 'Continuation of Box No. IV'). For indicating continuation/continuation-in-part of an earlier application, see MPEP § 1828.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request may include inventor declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application may include in the Request a declaration of the inventors as provided for in PCT Rule 4.17(iv).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including the declaration in the Request is optional but permitted; follow PCT Rule specifications when included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal fee handling and forwarding to the International Bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon payment of a fee equal to the transmittal fee, the USPTO will promptly transmit the international application to the International Bureau under PCT Rule 19.4(b) when acting as receiving Office on behalf of the IB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies when USPTO is receiving on behalf of IB under Rule 19.4(a), such as where applicants are not entitled to file in USRO but at least one applicant is a resident/national of any PCT Contracting State. Non-PCT-state applicants may not benefit from Rule 19.4.
